cards.title: Introduction to Next.js
cards.content:
Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. It provides production-ready features out of the box like routing, rendering optimizations, data fetching, and bundling, which means you don't need to manually configure Webpack or Babel.

Key highlights include:

  • App Router: A newer routing paradigm built on React Server Components.
  • Optimizations: Automated image, font, and script performance enhancements.
  • Server Actions: Direct database/mutation interaction without building an intermediate REST API.

cards.title: React Server vs. Client Components
cards.content:
In Next.js, components inside the app directory are React Server Components (RSC) by default.

  • Server Components: Render on the server. They reduce client bundle size since their dependencies are not sent to the browser. They can safely access databases or backend APIs directly.
  • Client Components: Rendered on the server initially (pre-rendered) and hydrated on the client. They are required if you need hooks (useState, useEffect), browser APIs, or interactive event listeners (onClick).
// Client Component declaration
"use client";

import { useState } from 'react';

export default function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>{count}</button>;
}

options.text: They are Client Components by default and require "use server" to run on the server.
They are Server Components by default and do not send JavaScript for rendering to the browser.
They run only on the database layer and cannot return JSX.
They are rendered purely on the client side without any server-side involvement.

cards.title: Routing in Next.js
cards.content:
Next.js uses a file-system based router where folders define the paths, and special files define the UI.

Some of the most important reserved filenames inside a route folder include:

  • page.js: Unique UI for the route (makes the path publicly accessible).
  • layout.js: Shared UI for a route segment and its children (preserves state on navigation).
  • loading.js: Fallback UI wrapper using React Suspense.
  • error.js: Error boundary wrapper for the segment.

cards.title: Data Fetching & Server Actions
cards.content:
Next.js extends the native fetch Web API to configure caching and revalidation directly on the server.

Additionally, Server Actions allow you to execute asynchronous code directly on the server without creating APIs.

// Example Server Component fetching data
async function getProjects() {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/projects', {
    next: { revalidate: 3600 } // cache for 1 hour
  });
  return res.json();
}

export default async function Dashboard() {
  const projects = await getProjects();
  return <div>{projects.map(p => <p>{p.name}</p>)}</div>;
}

cards.title: Static vs. Dynamic Rendering
cards.content:
Next.js automatically optimizes how routes are compiled:

  • Static Rendering: Routes are rendered at build time or in the background. Good for blogs, marketing pages, or pages where data is identical for all users.
  • Dynamic Rendering: Routes are rendered for each user at request time. This is triggered when Next.js detects dynamic functions (like cookies(), headers(), or searchParams) or uncached data fetches.

pairs.right: HTML created once during build time, served instantly via CDN.
HTML created on demand for each incoming request dynamically.
Recreates individual static pages in the background without rebuilds.
Browser downloads minimal HTML and populates DOM using JS.

cards.title: Built-in Optimization Features
cards.content:
Next.js features custom built-in React components that handle standard performance pitfalls:

  • next/image: Automatically resizes, compresses, and serves modern formats (like WebP) with layout shift protection.
  • next/link: Prefetches viewport-visible links in the background for instant navigation transition.
  • next/font: Automatically downloads and hosts Google Fonts locally during build time to eliminate layout shifts.

options.text: It converts all images into SVG formats automatically.
It resizes images, prevents Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), and lazy loads files by default.
It executes image compression using client-side WebAssembly after hydration.
It completely prevents the browser from loading images on mobile viewports to save data.
